experiment: E13 — tuning the LoRA judge: both orders averaged, swap-augmented training, balanced verdict weights (free, on the gaming PC)
written_at: 2026-10-18T17:30:00Z, before any E13 call or training run
why: E11/E12: C4 doubles social kappa over the untrained model, flattens after a third of the data, and its misses are not near-decisions (a cut on P(na) does not recover them). The levers left are how it is asked and how it is taught, not more of the same data.

literature.position_bias: Pairwise LLM judges change verdicts when the two items are swapped (MT-Bench, Zheng et al. 2023; 'Judging the Judges', arXiv 2406.07791); the standard check asks both orders and keeps what survives the swap.
literature.swap_augmentation: JudgeLM (Zhu et al., ICLR 2025, arXiv 2310.17631) fine-tunes judges on teacher verdicts with the two answers swapped and the teacher's verdict swapped with them, to make the student attend to content, not position.
literature.class_weighting: LLM-labelled training for stance and ideology classifiers (e.g. RED-CT, arXiv 2408.08217) weights the rare classes; here 'na' is 72-85 % of verdicts.
literature.after_e13: Judge-aware Bradley-Terry (BT-sigma, arXiv 2602.16610) and prediction-powered ranking (arXiv 2402.17826) combine a cheap noisy judge with a small set from a better one and keep the intervals valid — the route if the local judge stays noisier than gpt-5.4-mini.

candidates.C4-S: C4 (E11's adapter, unchanged) read in both orders; the two orders' probabilities averaged (the second's A/B swapped back); the likeliest option per axis, econ first (pipeline.judge.client.SwapJudge). No tuning.
candidates.C5: retrained like C4 (same base, LoRA, optimiser, steps, checkpoint rule) on b1 + E10 with every training example also shown A/B-swapped, its verdict letters swapped (infra/pc/train_lora.py --swap-augment). One epoch over the doubled set = the same 386 steps as C4.
candidates.C6: C5 plus balanced verdict weights: on each axis, the verdict token of an A or B answer weighs n_na / n_decided of the training set (so decided and 'na' answers carry equal total weight); validation loss, which picks the checkpoint, stays unweighted (--decided-weight balanced).
candidates.C5-S, C6-S: C5 and C6 read in both orders, as C4-S.

test: E9's harness, unchanged: the same 943 test calls; J1 agreement, Cohen's kappa, flip/miss/invent, J3 positions rho. Also reported: order consistency — the share of calls whose single-order answer is the same in both orders.
choice: The pilot's judge = the candidate with the highest mean of the two axes' kappa on E9. A candidate replaces C4 only if its social kappa is at least 0.03 above C4's (0.40); otherwise C4 stays (smaller differences are within the noise of 943 calls and of repeated runs, E12).
rules: No change to data, settings, test or metrics after seeing any E13 result. Validation days are used only to pick each run's checkpoint, as in E11. No claims (pipeline phase).
amended: 2026-10-18 ~18:55 CEST, before any C5/C6 training step: to cut GPU time (4 h → ≈ 1.5 h), C5 and C6 train on the first third of the training days (--days-share 0.333; ≈ 1,300 examples, doubled by the swap), one epoch over the doubled set, and are compared with C4-1/3 (same days; social kappa 0.38) instead of C4. Choice rule unchanged otherwise: a winner needs social kappa ≥ C4-1/3's + 0.03; it is then retrained on all days or used as is.
amended_2: 2026-10-18 20:16 CEST, before any C5/C6 test result: C6 stacked the weights on the swap, so it could not show what the weights do alone. It was stopped at step ~60 and never tested. C7 replaces it: C4-1/3's recipe (first third of the days, 2 epochs, 164 steps) plus balanced verdict weights, no swap. Each change is now tested alone against C4-1/3: C5 = swap only, C7 = weights only; the same rule (social kappa ≥ C4-1/3's 0.38 + 0.03).
amended_3: 2026-10-19 07:15 CEST, before any Gemma call or training step: the same four arms on Gemma 4 12B (Google, 2026; A73). G1 = untrained (served: google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct, thinking off, temperature 0); G4-1/3, G5, G7 = C4-1/3's, C5's and C7's recipes unchanged (same days, epochs, steps, LoRA settings, checkpoint rule), trained on google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized quantised to NF4 on load, as the Qwen base was. One difference forced by the model: Gemma's 8 full-attention layers use one projection for keys and values, which vLLM cannot serve a LoRA on as trained, so those 8 k_proj are left out of the LoRA. Test and metrics unchanged (E9). Within Gemma, a variant beats G4-1/3 by the same rule (social kappa >= G4-1/3's + 0.03). Across models, Gemma replaces Qwen as the judge only if its best variant's social kappa is >= the best Qwen variant's + 0.03.
